agencies.name: Ministry of Environment
agencies.role: Runs a nationwide network that directly measures pollutants such as PM2.5 and publishes official readings.

monitoring.text: In March 2026 the Ministry reported an average PM2.5 of 25.32 µg/m³ for the 24 hours to 07:00 on 29 March, which it called good and below its 50 µg/m³ standard.
The Ministry disputed IQAir figures, saying satellite data and modelling may not capture local conditions and may misread humidity or fog as pollution.

seasonalPattern.text: GGGI notes that pollution levels in Cambodia are often highest in the dry season.

policy.text: GGGI published a situation assessment of Cambodia's air quality monitoring under the AFD-funded Air Quality Improvement Program, saying the monitoring system needs strengthening.

openQuestions: Cambodia's Ministry of Environment cites a 50 µg/m³ PM2.5 standard and a nationwide network, but the station count, any banded index and where readings are published have not been established.
GGGI's full assessment report has not been reviewed.
